title: MCP Architecture Under the Hood

host executes tool on local mcp server

caption:
Your MCP tools don't talk directly to Claude. Here's what actually happens when an LLM uses MCP:

1. LLM API — Claude never runs code directly; it only returns a JSON request.

2. MCP Host — Applications like Cursor or Claude Desktop receive the request and act as the orchestrator.

3. MCP Server — The host forwards requests via stdio or SSE to a local process.

4. Local DB — The MCP server queries resources securely outside the LLM. When building AI tool integrations, remember MCP is a client-side protocol that protects credentials. No magic — just RPC over local transport.
